contract: Ordered native runtime values through the existing NativeObservation and strict source decoder. Host errors retain separate complete source and Rust assertions.
compared: Every case: projected complete runtime value and verifierResult, including own-undefined values and opaque function identities.
Every case: outcome.returned; complete successful outcome.result; sameOriginal strict identity on every failure.
Every non-host failure: complete error name/message and own properties, including order and original thrown object values.
Every case: complete ordered events, projection input, custom verifier hash/password arguments and sameHash, split method receiver identity and complete arguments.
Every case: function identity registration order and errorFunctions (empty in all 24 cases).
Every case: all stored user/session/account/verification/twoFactor rows, row order, every field, own-undefined values, Date values, and field order.
Every runtime object and array: source own-key and descriptor order validated by the strict shared decoder; runtime key order and array length compared by assert_replay.
Host failures: name and complete message are compared across runtimes for all four cases; complete per-host error observations are asserted separately.

notCompared.reason: Rust functions do not expose JavaScript source reflection. All source values remain in the frozen fixture.

Function snapshots cross the explicit opaque function boundary. Function identities, split receiver identity, and verifier sameHash are compared. JavaScript prototype/constructor cycles remain in the source fixture.

The existing runtime observer compares values and order without general allocation labels. The 24-case fixture has six references, all in excluded function prototype metadata; no runtime object reference is discarded.
FieldObject exposes enumerable state, not JavaScript writable/configurable flags. These flags remain in the frozen fixture.
Bun attaches source location properties. Rust errors have no JavaScript source location. Both complete observations are preserved and separately asserted in hostErrors.
